name: manual_d7f233
claim: An agent renaming a directory/binary must never also infer a broader identity change (module path, package namespace, org identity) in the same commit unless explicitly authorized — each identity-bearing change needs its own explicit human sign-off, even when bundled with an authorized structural rename. When citing live go.mod values after such an incident, verify each repository independently: GitHub repo lineage (wesm/agentsview redirects to kenn-io/agentsview) does not imply a fork already adopted the parent vanity module path.

decisions.notes: Correction for lesson_0c339d39a80c (PR #321 / CodeRabbit + owner clarification 2026-08-03). Live re-verify at remediation time: kenn-io/agentsview declares module go.kenn.io/agentsview; latentsignal-org/periscope@main still declares module github.com/wesm/agentsview; github.com/wesm/agentsview HTTP-redirects to kenn-io/agentsview (same repo lineage after the wesm→kenn-io rename). Upstream vanity migration is commit 6ef281c74db5 ("Use go.kenn.io vanity module path"); the latentsignal fork never received that go.mod change. The original 0c339d39a80c notes incorrectly stated that latentsignal-org/periscope@main also declares go.kenn.io/agentsview — aedbe2d7db06 was correct that the fork still has github.com/wesm/agentsview. HITL claim stands; only the live-path evidence needed this append-only supersession. Unauthorized invented path github.com/latentsignal-org/periscope remains absent from both live trees.
